messages:
matt-support: Heads-up — ACME reported intermittent TLS failures to our Private API after a cert rotation at 02:03 UTC. They see 502/504s and client errors: "x509: certificate signed by unknown authority". Asking for repro steps.

jane-acme: We started seeing it right after your rotator finished. From our app host inside the VPC, curl to our service fails; from a cloud VM it succeeds. :confused: 

matt-support: Snippet from their app host logs:

``
Mar 14 02:12:10 app[web]: TLS handshake error: x509: certificate signed by unknown authority
Mar 14 02:12:10 app[web]: verify: depth=1, subject="CN=redwood-intermediate", issuer="CN=redwood-root"
```

rotator-bot: rotation event: tenant=acme, completed_at=2026-03-14T02:03:02Z, new_intermediate=redwood-intermediate-2026-03-14, ocsp_uri=https://ocsp.intca.example/ocsp

ana-netops: Do they have egress to the OCSP responder? If stapling isn't being honored, their clients will try to fetch OCSP from inside the VPC. Need to verify connectivity to the OCSP host/IP.

jane-acme: Ran curl from the app host, it timed out:

``
$ curl -v https://ocsp.intca.example/ocsp
*   Trying 198.51.100.23:443...
* connect to 198.51.100.23 port 443 failed: Connection timed out
```

devon-eng: 198.51.100.23 is the OCSP responder IP. Is that IP in ACME's allowlist for their NAT egress? If their NAT public IP changed, their firewall rules may be blocking the responder.

chris-sre: Also check for an outbound proxy or explicit deny rules. Ask for `traceroute`, `ip route`, and a tcpdump to show packets.

matt-support: They ran traceroute -> we see an early * (dropped) and tcpdump showing SYNs without SYN-ACKs. Looks like egress is blackholed.

jane-acme: We recently replaced our NAT gateway at 01:58 UTC and our public SNAT changed. Our security team has a tight egress ACL that only allows a short list of external IPs.

ana-netops: So two likely causes: 1) their outbound IP changed and the customer's ACL denied the OCSP responder, or 2) the customer's firewall blocks that responder or port. Packet capture indicates no SYN-ACKs, so upstream filtering is probable.

devon-eng: Short-term fix: allow the OCSP responder IPs (198.51.100.23, 198.51.100.24) in their egress list or open the responder hostname. We also suggested verifying that our stapling is present, but note some clients still perform OCSP fetches.

chris-sre: Provided quick test commands to allow egress locally or update cloud ACLs:

``
# quick allow for testing
sudo iptables -I OUTPUT 1 -d 198.51.100.23 -j ACCEPT
sudo iptables -I OUTPUT 1 -d 198.51.100.24 -j ACCEPT
# or add 198.51.100.0/24 to cloud egress allowlist
```

jane-acme: Added the OCSP IPs to our allowlist and restarted. `curl https://ocsp.intca.example/ocsp` now returns HTTP/200. App handshakes returned to normal. :tada:

chris-sre: One extra note — customer had an HAProxy reload that previously dropped the intermediate cert (they had a truncated chain uploaded). We validated and reuploaded the full chain via our support UI as a precaution.

matt-support: Closing the ticket after ACME confirmed recovery. Follow-ups: add OCSP responder IPs/hosts to our Private/VPC onboarding doc, add a rotator post-rotation checklist for customers that run restrictive egress ACLs, and add a rotator log warning when common egress IPs may be affected by rotation.

ana-netops: I'll draft the checklist and a short KB article about NAT changes and OCSP egress requirements.

devon-eng: Filed internal task to emit a rotator advisory if we detect a change that might require customers to update egress ACLs.

matt-support: Thanks all — ticket closed. :thumbsup:
